headline: Sputnik reached orbit, federal troops walked nine students into Little Rock Central High, and Ghana became independent
texture: George Metesky, charged with planting more than thirty bombs around New York City, was arrested in Waterbury on January 22. Ku Klux Klan members forced the truck driver Willie Edwards off a bridge into the Alabama River the next day and he drowned. A coal gas explosion at the Bishop mine in Virginia killed 37 men on February 4, and a fire at a home for the elderly in Warrenton, Missouri killed 72 on February 17. Hurricane Audrey demolished Cameron, Louisiana on June 27, killing 400.

The floodgates of The Dalles Dam closed on March 10 and drowned Celilo Falls and the Native American fisheries along that stretch of the Columbia River. Oklahoma marked its semi-centennial of statehood on June 15 by burying a new Plymouth Belvedere in a time capsule, to be dug up in fifty years. Toyota began exporting to the United States on October 31, starting with the Toyota Crown. The FBI arrested Jimmy Hoffa on March 13 and charged him with bribery.

Dedan Kimathi was executed by the British colonial government in Kenya on February 18, the day Walter James Bolton was hanged at Mount Eden in the last execution carried out in New Zealand. Heavy rain and mudslides at Isahaya in western Kyushu killed 992 people in July. The sailing ship Pamir went down off the Azores in a hurricane on September 21. Sukarno survived a grenade thrown at the Cikini School in Jakarta on November 30, which killed six children, and 326,000 Dutch nationals were expelled from Indonesia five days later.

Paul Robeson, blacklisted from travelling outside the United States, sang down the new transatlantic telephone line from New York to an audience at St Pancras Town Hall in London on May 26, and used the same line on October 5 to address the Miners' Eisteddfod at the Grand Pavilion in Porthcawl. Dalida took the first gold record awarded in France, for 300,000 sales of Bambino. Three neo-grotesque sans-serif typefaces came out, Folio, Neue Haas Grotesk and Univers. The last new case of Chinese foot binding was reported.

pol.us_president.label: US President
pol.us_president.detail: Richard Nixon was Vice President, Earl Warren was Chief Justice, Sam Rayburn was Speaker of the House and Lyndon B. Johnson was Senate majority leader. The 85th Congress sat from January 3. Eisenhower suffered a stroke on November 25.

pol.inauguration.label: Eisenhower sworn in for a second term
pol.inauguration.value: Took the oath privately at the White House on Sunday January 20, with the public ceremony at the East Portico of the Capitol the following day
pol.inauguration.detail: Earl Warren administered the presidential oath after Senate minority leader William Knowland swore in Richard Nixon. Marian Anderson sang the national anthem, the first African American woman to perform at a presidential inauguration. The US year page gives only January 20 and does not mention the two ceremonies.

pol.little_rock.label: Little Rock Central High School
pol.little_rock.value: Governor Orval Faubus called out the National Guard to stop the nine African American students known as the Little Rock Nine from enrolling, and Eisenhower sent federal troops on September 24 to give them safe passage into the building
pol.little_rock.detail: The US year page spells the governor Orville in this entry and Orval in its list of governors.

pol.dover_apology.label: Eisenhower apologises to Ghana's finance minister
pol.dover_apology.value: Made the apology after the minister was refused service in a restaurant in Dover, Delaware
pol.dover_apology.detail: The US year page spells his name Komla Agbeli Gbdemah, so the fact describes him by office rather than repeating a spelling that looks mistyped.

pol.civil_rights_act.label: Civil Rights Act of 1957
pol.civil_rights_act.value: Enacted, establishing the United States Commission on Civil Rights
pol.civil_rights_act.detail: Senator Strom Thurmond had spoken against a civil rights bill for 24 hours and 18 minutes from August 28, the longest filibuster on record. The Royal Ice Cream sit-in took place on June 23.

pol.eisenhower_doctrine.label: Eisenhower Doctrine approved
pol.eisenhower_doctrine.value: Congress backed assistance to foreign regimes threatened by Communism
pol.eisenhower_doctrine.detail: Eisenhower announced a two-year suspension of nuclear testing on August 21. The Gaither Report of November 7 called for more American missiles and fallout shelters.

world.sputnik.label: Sputnik 1 launched
world.sputnik.value: The Soviet Union put the first artificial satellite into orbit around the Earth
world.sputnik.detail: Sputnik 2 went up on November 3 carrying a dog named Laika, the first animal to orbit the Earth, with no technology available to bring her back. The orbit of the last stage of the R-7 rocket that carried Sputnik was first calculated on an IBM 704 at the MIT Computation Center on October 11, as part of Operation Moonwatch. The International Geophysical Year had begun on July 1, and the International Atomic Energy Agency was established on July 29.

world.treaty_of_rome.label: Treaty of Rome
world.treaty_of_rome.value: Italy, France, West Germany, Belgium, the Netherlands and Luxembourg established the European Economic Community
world.treaty_of_rome.detail: The Saarland had joined West Germany on January 1.

world.ghana.label: Ghana independent
world.ghana.value: The British colonies of the Gold Coast and British Togoland became Ghana, the first country in colonial Africa to gain independence
world.ghana.detail: Tunisia became a republic on July 25 with Habib Bourguiba as its first president. The Federation of Malaya left the United Kingdom on August 31, its constitution having come into force on August 27, and Abdul Rahman of Negeri Sembilan became the first Yang di-Pertuan Agong.

world.macmillan.label: Harold Macmillan becomes Prime Minister
world.macmillan.value: Took over in the United Kingdom the day after Anthony Eden resigned on health grounds
world.macmillan.detail: Egypt reopened the Suez Canal on March 8 and reopened it to all shipping on April 9. Israel had withdrawn from the Sinai Peninsula on January 20.

world.windscale.label: Windscale fire
world.windscale.value: A fire at the Windscale nuclear reactor on the north-west coast of England released radioactive material into the surrounding environment, including iodine-131
world.windscale.detail: Britain had tested its first hydrogen bomb at Malden Island in the Pacific on May 15, under Operation Grapple, and the device failed to detonate properly. The Kyshtym disaster at the Mayak nuclear reprocessing plant in Russia occurred on September 29.

world.lewisham.label: Lewisham rail crash
world.lewisham.value: Two trains collided in London and 92 people died
world.lewisham.detail: The same page's opening caption puts the toll at 90 rather than 92. A flying boat crash on the Isle of Wight had left 45 dead on November 15, and two trains colliding at Yarimburgaz in Turkey killed 95 on October 20.

film.gross.label: Highest-grossing films, US domestic rentals
value: The Bridge on the River Kwai, $15,000,000, Columbia
Peyton Place, $11,000,000, 20th Century Fox
Sayonara, $10,500,000, Warner Bros.
Search for Paradise, $6,500,000, Cinerama Releasing
Old Yeller, $5,900,000, Buena Vista
film.gross.detail: Rentals, the distributor share rather than the ticket window total, so roughly half what a gross figure would say. The same page's country table puts The Bridge on the River Kwai at $27,200,000 and 54,400,000 admissions in the United States and Canada, citing Box Office Mojo, against the $15,000,000 rentals figure here. Mother India took the highest gross in India at 80,000,000 rupees on 100,000,000 admissions.

film.best_picture.label: Best Picture
film.best_picture.value: The Bridge on the River Kwai
film.best_picture.detail: Awarded the following spring at the 30th Academy Awards, where it won seven awards and Sayonara led on nominations with ten. Best Adapted Screenplay went to Pierre Boulle, who did not speak English, because the writers Carl Foreman and Michael Wilson were blacklisted and had taken no screen credit. For the first time under the five-nominee rule, the Best Director nominees matched the Best Picture nominees exactly.

film.acting_awards.label: Acting Oscars
value: Best Actor, Alec Guinness, The Bridge on the River Kwai
Best Actress, Joanne Woodward, The Three Faces of Eve
Best Supporting Actor, Red Buttons, Sayonara
Best Supporting Actress, Miyoshi Umeki, Sayonara
film.acting_awards.detail: Peyton Place took nine nominations and won nothing, tying the record for most nominations without a win, and five of those nine were acting nominations. Woodward made her own dress for the ceremony, which prompted the presenter Joan Crawford to say she was setting the cause of Hollywood glamour back twenty years by making her own clothes.

film.world_cinema.label: Notable films from elsewhere
value: Throne of Blood, directed by Akira Kurosawa, Japan
The Seventh Seal, directed by Ingmar Bergman, Sweden
Nights of Cabiria, directed by Federico Fellini, Italy
Mother India, directed by Mehboob Khan, India
The Cranes Are Flying, directed by Mikhail Kalatozov, Soviet Union
film.world_cinema.detail: Throne of Blood, a reworking of Macbeth, opened in Japan on January 15 and The Seventh Seal opened in Sweden on February 16. Nights of Cabiria won the Academy Award for Best Foreign Language Film. Bergman's Wild Strawberries was released in Sweden on December 6.

film.how_people_watched.label: How people watched
film.how_people_watched.value: In a theatre. The fourth title in the rentals table, Search for Paradise, came from Cinerama Releasing, and Raintree County was the first film shot in MGM Camera 65 when it opened on October 2.
film.how_people_watched.detail: RKO stopped distributing feature films in the United States on February 1 and Universal took the business over. The first London Film Festival opened at the newly built National Film Theatre on October 16.

tv.top_shows.label: Most-watched programs, season starting autumn 1957
value: Gunsmoke, CBS, 43.1 rating
The Danny Thomas Show, CBS, 35.3
Tales of Wells Fargo, NBC, 35.2
Have Gun Will Travel, CBS, 33.7
I've Got a Secret, CBS, 33.4
tv.top_shows.detail: Nielsen reports by season, so this ranking covers the season that began in the autumn and ran into the following spring. Westerns took five of the top eight places, the three above plus The Life and Legend of Wyatt Earp at six and The Restless Gun at eight.

tv.premieres.label: Programs that debuted
value: Have Gun Will Travel, CBS, September 14
Wagon Train, NBC, September 18
Perry Mason, CBS, September 21
Maverick, ABC, September 22
Leave It to Beaver, CBS, October 4
Zorro, ABC, October 10
tv.premieres.detail: Steve Allen made his last appearance as host of Tonight on January 25, the show was recast as Tonight! America After Dark under Jack Lescoulie, and Jack Paar took over as permanent host from the July 29 episode. The 180th and final first-run episode of I Love Lucy was filmed at Desilu Studios on April 4 and broadcast on May 6.

tv.american_bandstand.label: American Bandstand joins ABC
tv.american_bandstand.value: A local dance show produced by WFIL-TV in Philadelphia went out on the ABC Television Network

tv.nat_king_cole.label: Nat King Cole's series and the colour line
tv.nat_king_cole.value: With no sponsor willing to back the show, Frankie Laine gave up his usual fee of $10,000 to become the first white artist to appear as a guest
tv.nat_king_cole.detail: Mel Torme and Tony Bennett followed him on. The ratings rose and the show still failed to find a national sponsor.

tv.production_moves.label: Where prime time was made
tv.production_moves.value: Hollywood overtook New York as the dominant city for filming prime time programs, and live broadcasts gave way to filmed series
tv.production_moves.detail: Westinghouse introduced the first rectangular tube colour television and withdrew the sets over trouble aligning the guns to get a single image. NBC put out its first animated version of the living colour peacock logo on September 7, on that day's episode of Your Hit Parade.

radio.today.label: Today begins on the BBC
radio.today.value: First broadcast as a daily early-morning topical programme on the BBC Home Service
radio.today.detail: KPEG in Spokane, Washington had gone on air on February 12 with an all-woman announcing team, every member using the first name Peg on air.

radio.network_closings.label: Network radio programmes ending
radio.network_closings.value: Hilltop House ended on NBC on July 30, CBS Radio Workshop ended on September 22, and Strike It Rich ended on NBC on December 27
radio.network_closings.detail: The Crime Files of Flamond had ended on Mutual on February 27 and Official Detective on March 7.

music.chart_toppers.label: Records that reached number one
value: All Shook Up, Elvis Presley, 8 weeks from April 13
Teddy Bear, Elvis Presley, 7 weeks from July 8
Jailhouse Rock, Elvis Presley, 7 weeks from October 21
Love Letters in the Sand, Pat Boone, 5 weeks from June 3
Young Love, Tab Hunter, 4 weeks from March 2
music.chart_toppers.detail: From Billboard's charts, ordered by weeks at the top. The table lists seventeen runs at number one, the first of them Presley's Too Much from February 9, and Tammy returning for a second turn in September. Presley took four of those runs and held the top spot for 25 weeks between them.

music.west_side_story.label: West Side Story opens on Broadway
music.west_side_story.value: Music by Leonard Bernstein and lyrics by Stephen Sondheim, at the Winter Garden Theatre
music.west_side_story.detail: Sondheim's Broadway debut, after tryouts in Washington and Philadelphia from August. Bernstein was appointed music director of the New York Philharmonic a week later.

music.rock_banned.label: Rock and roll banned from Chicago Catholic schools
music.rock_banned.value: Cardinal Stritch barred all rock and roll and rhythm and blues from Catholic-run schools, saying that its rhythms encourage young people to behave in a hedonistic manner

music.quarrymen.label: Lennon and McCartney meet
music.quarrymen.value: Paul McCartney, aged fifteen, met John Lennon at a fete at St Peter's Church in Woolton, where Lennon's skiffle group the Quarrymen were playing
music.quarrymen.detail: The Cavern Club had opened in Liverpool on January 16 as a jazz club. The Quarrymen played there on August 7 in an interval spot between jazz bands, and when Lennon started the group on Presley's Don't Be Cruel the owner handed him a note reading cut out the bloody rock 'n roll.

music.graceland.label: Elvis Presley buys Graceland
music.graceland.value: Paid $100,000 for the house at 3734 Bellevue Boulevard in Memphis and moved his family there from 1034 Audubon Drive
music.graceland.detail: No date is given here because the sources disagree. The US year page dates the purchase to March 26 and gives the price, the address and Presley's age of 22. The music page dates it to March 19 and gives none of those.

tech.fortran.label: First Fortran compiler
tech.fortran.value: IBM began selling the first compiler for the Fortran scientific programming language
tech.fortran.detail: Hugh Everett III published the first scientifically founded many-worlds interpretation of quantum mechanics on July 1.

tech.vanguard.label: First US satellite attempt fails
tech.vanguard.value: The Vanguard rocket blew up on the launch pad
tech.vanguard.detail: Shippingport Atomic Power Station went onstream on December 2.

tech.boeing_707.label: Boeing 707 first flight
tech.boeing_707.value: The airliner flew for the first time
tech.boeing_707.detail: Major John Glenn of the United States Marines had flown an F8U supersonic jet from California to New York on July 16 in 3 hours, 23 minutes and 8 seconds, a transcontinental speed record.

tech.electric_watch.label: First electric watch
tech.electric_watch.value: The Hamilton Watch Company introduced it

tech.jodrell_bank.label: Jodrell Bank under its own control
tech.jodrell_bank.value: The radio telescope in Cheshire was controlled from its own control room for the first time

prices.gas.label: Average US gas price
prices.gas.detail: Leaded regular, US city average, including taxes, annual average.

prices.min_wage.label: Federal minimum wage
prices.min_wage.detail: The basic rate for covered nonfarm workers, as in effect on December 31.

culture.mood.label: Mood
culture.mood.value: Soviet satellites overhead from October, federal troops walking children into an Arkansas high school, and westerns filling most of the evening on television.

culture.on_the_road.label: On the Road published
culture.on_the_road.value: Viking Press published Jack Kerouac's novel
culture.on_the_road.detail: Copies of Allen Ginsberg's Howl and Other Poems printed in Britain were seized by US Customs officials in San Francisco on March 25 on grounds of obscenity. Ayn Rand's Atlas Shrugged was published on October 10.

culture.nobel_prizes.label: Nobel Prizes
value: Literature, Albert Camus
Peace, Lester B. Pearson
Physics, Chen-Ning Yang and Tsung-Dao Lee
Chemistry, Alexander R. Todd
Physiology or Medicine, Daniel Bovet
culture.nobel_prizes.detail: Pearson, a Canadian diplomat, received his prize on December 10 for his peacekeeping efforts at the United Nations.

culture.edsel.label: Ford introduces the Edsel
culture.edsel.value: Launched on what the company proclaimed as E Day
culture.edsel.detail: The Mackinac Bridge, the longest suspension bridge between anchorages at the time, opened on November 1 and connected Michigan's two peninsulas. Standard and Poor's first published the S&P 500 index on March 4.

culture.apalachin.label: Apalachin meeting
culture.apalachin.value: American Mafia leaders met at Joseph Barbara's house in Apalachin, New York, and a curious patrolman broke the meeting up
culture.apalachin.detail: Albert Anastasia had been shot dead in a barber shop at the Park Sheraton Hotel in New York City on October 25. Edward Gein killed Bernice Worden of Plainfield, Wisconsin on November 16.

sports.world_series.label: World Series
sports.world_series.value: Milwaukee Braves beat the New York Yankees four games to three, their second title

sports.franchise_moves.label: Two New York clubs leave for California
sports.franchise_moves.value: Horace Stoneham announced on August 19 that the Giants were moving to San Francisco, and Walter O'Malley announced on October 8 that the Dodgers were moving to Los Angeles
sports.franchise_moves.detail: O'Malley had agreed to the move on May 3. Jackie Robinson retired on January 5 rather than move across town to the Giants, who had traded for him.

sports.gibson.label: Althea Gibson at Wimbledon
sports.gibson.value: Beat Darlene Hard 6-3, 6-2 to become the first black player to win a Wimbledon singles championship
sports.gibson.detail: She also beat Louise Brough 6-3, 6-2 for the American women's singles championship, and was named Associated Press Female Athlete of the Year. Ted Williams took the male award.

sports.f1.label: Formula One World Championship
sports.f1.value: Juan Manuel Fangio took a fifth drivers' championship, his fourth in a row, clinching it with four wins in the season at the German Grand Prix for Maserati

sports.champions.label: Other championships
value: NFL Championship, Detroit Lions 59, Cleveland Browns 14, at Briggs Stadium
Stanley Cup, Montreal Canadiens over the Boston Bruins, four games to one
NBA Finals, Boston Celtics over the St. Louis Hawks, four games to three
European Cup, Real Madrid over Fiorentina, 2 to 0
NCAA basketball, North Carolina over Kansas, 54 to 53
World middleweight title, Carmen Basilio over Sugar Ray Robinson on a 15-round decision
sports.champions.detail: Basilio won on September 23. Auburn was voted national champion in college football by the AP poll and played no bowl game because of sanctions. Roy Sievers led the American League with 42 home runs and 114 runs batted in for the last-place Washington Senators, and Warren Spahn of the Braves took the Cy Young Award.

deaths.bogart.label: Humphrey Bogart
deaths.bogart.detail: American actor, of Casablanca and The Maltese Falcon, who died of esophageal cancer in Los Angeles at 57.

deaths.sibelius.label: Jean Sibelius
deaths.sibelius.detail: Finnish composer, aged 91, who had completed no significant compositions for thirty years. He died at his home Ainola while a performance of his Symphony No. 5 was being given in Helsinki under Malcolm Sargent.

notes: Research pass July 2026, from the cached wikitext under .sources/1957. figures_basis is rentals: the box office table's column header reads Domestic rentals. The same film page's country table gives a much larger gross and an admissions count for The Bridge on the River Kwai, and both bases are named in the film.gross detail rather than reconciled. Source disagreements labelled rather than resolved: the Graceland purchase is March 26 on the US year page, with price and address, and March 19 on the music page, so music.graceland carries no date; the US year page spells the Arkansas governor Orville in the September 4 entry and Orval in its list of governors, and pol.little_rock uses Orval and says so; the year page's body puts the Lewisham rail crash toll at 92 and its opening caption at 90, and world.lewisham uses 92 and names the gap. The inauguration was checked against its own article because January 20 fell on a Sunday: the oath was taken privately at the White House that day and the public ceremony was held at the Capitol on January 21, which the US year page does not mention, so pol.inauguration cites https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_inauguration_of_Dwight_D._Eisenhower and names the gap. The Ghana finance minister refused service in Dover, Delaware is spelled Komla Agbeli Gbdemah on the US year page, which looks like a typo, so the fact describes him by office and quotes the page's spelling instead of correcting it. The Nielsen ranking is a season starting in the autumn of 1957 and running into the following spring, which the fact says without naming a second year. No Hot 100 fact, because Billboard did not start that chart in this year; music.chart_toppers comes from the Billboard charts of the time. No film.ticket_price fact, because the ticket price series has no value for this year. Dropped for lack of a settled or usable source: the year page's claim that the influenza pandemic killed over a million people worldwide, which appears only in the lead image caption and spans two years; the Africanized bee release in Brazil and the Gordion tumulus excavation, both untagged and undated; Gordon Gould inventing the laser on November 13, which the page supports only with an article about his birth; the Royal Ice Cream sit-in, which the US year page lists with no description at all and which is therefore named without one in the pol.civil_rights_act detail. Texture material taken from the cached pages but not given its own fact: George Metesky's arrest in Waterbury; Willie Edwards and the Alabama River; the Bishop mine explosion; the Warrenton fire; Hurricane Audrey; The Dalles Dam and Celilo Falls; the Oklahoma time capsule; Toyota's first US exports; Jimmy Hoffa's arrest; Dedan Kimathi and Walter James Bolton; the Isahaya mudslides; the Pamir; the Cikini School grenade and the expulsion of Dutch nationals; Paul Robeson's telephone concerts; Dalida's gold record; Folio, Neue Haas Grotesk and Univers; the last reported case of Chinese foot binding. Two facts draw a date from one cached page and their detail from another, which is recorded here rather than left for a reader to notice. deaths.sibelius takes the date and birth year from the year page and takes Ainola, the age of 91 and the Helsinki performance of the Symphony No. 5 from the music page. sports.champions takes the six results and the Auburn line from the sports page, and the entry for the European Cup drops the venue and date, the Santiago Bernabeu on May 30, because only the year page carries them. General knowledge rather than a claim from the cached pages: that a cinema audience of this period saw films in a theatre first and on television later, which film.how_people_watched implies without stating. Deaths carry a birth year rather than an age except where the source gives an age outright, matching the neighbouring files. Names and titles are written in ASCII per the corpus convention, so Yarimburgaz, Mel Torme and Have Gun Will Travel lose their diacritics and dash. Review pass promoted the Jodrell Bank control room out of tech.electric_watch into its own fact; the two share a year and nothing else.
